slice: A35 — correlated request/job evidence, truthful playback-source QoE, retention and redaction
verdict: OPS-02 flips to PASS. One browser walk (upload -> transcode -> HLS playback -> search) is followed end to end on named id fields; all three services log structured JSON and a 15-check secret sweep over 22 artefacts found nothing; a real worker failure appears on the admin surfaces and moves the queue gauge; every metric label space is bounded and stayed bounded under a 120-distinct-URL probe; QoE classifies a real api-proxy playback correctly and refuses a client-claimed source; every retention window was run and observed. Four id-drop hops and one metrics-visibility gap are recorded, three defects are fixed.

prs.dependency_order: independent — no OpenAPI change and no migration in any of the three, so contract-ci has no ordering to respect. core schema stays 135, search stays 18.

lab.topology: one origin — a pipe-only node proxy on 127.0.0.1:8099 in front of `node .next/standalone/server.js` on :3100 and vidra-core api on :8088; a second vidra-core VIDRA_ROLE=worker with no listener; vidra-search on :8090
lab.postgres: native PostgreSQL 16.15 on 55432 (-k /tmp), fresh cluster, core schema 135, search schema 18
lab.redis: native redis on 56379 (core db 0, search db 1), flushed at start
lab.otel: a real collector — mirror.gcr.io/otel/opentelemetry-collector-contrib:0.160.0 (Docker Hub hangs here; the gcr mirror works), OTLP gRPC on 4317 for core and OTLP HTTP on 4318 for @vercel/otel, exporting to a file so spans could be read back
lab.browser: real Chromium (Playwright 1.62.1) against the proxy origin, hard reload between admin states
lab.fixture: a real ffmpeg clip — testsrc2 640x360 25fps 6s + a 440Hz sine, H.264/AAC, 589,668 bytes, sha256 135c1c30f5fd66ea9e97039f518c15ba750c9a1c97300b4195fd2fd4d3a57939
lab.rate_limits: RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED=false, so this lab says nothing about the shipped limits
lab.transcode_floor: TRANSCODING_MIN_FREE_SCRATCH_MB=512 — this box had 4.7 GiB free against the shipped 10 GiB floor, which would otherwise refuse every claim
lab.teardown: core api + worker, the Next standalone server, both lab proxies, vidra-search, redis and postgres stopped; the OTel container removed; the lab directory, its postgres cluster, the media root and the built binaries removed

sc2_safe_logs.verdict: PASS, with one defect fixed and one inconsistency recorded

schema.core: slog JSON: time, level, msg, plus per-line fields. A request line is method, path (the ROUTE TEMPLATE, never the raw URI), status, latency_ms, request_id, correlation_id, and trace_id/span_id when a trace is active
schema.vidra-search: the same handler (TWIN of core's NewLogger) — method, path, status, latency_ms, request_id, correlation_id. No trace_id: the service has no OTel
schema.vidra-user: lib/logger.ts, JSON with level/msg/time plus fields, and a RUNTIME redaction denylist (substring match on password/token/authorization/cookie/secret/apikey/session/totp/otp/private_key)

sc2_safe_logs.guards: core TestNoForbiddenLogging PASS, TestNoSensitiveLogKeys PASS. vidra-search ships NEITHER; measured with a ported copy of both AST walks — 0 forbidden diagnostic calls and 0 of its 32 distinct structured-log keys on core's denylist

sweep.detail: 9 literal values (the JWT secret, the internal HMAC secret, both KEKs, three account passwords, both DSNs) and 6 patterns (a postgres://redis:// scheme, a JWT, a credential key with a value, an email address, a bare storage key, a raw non-loopback IPv4) across every core/search/next/proxy log, seven captured admin and public response bodies, and three metrics scrapes

sc2_safe_logs.storage_key_fix: A17 recorded that jobstatus.RedactDetail did not strip a bare storage key and that the same text now reaches the WORKER LOG. Fixed here: the worker's five failure lines read `media: ffprobe "[redacted-key]" failed: exit status 1`, the admin failure list shows the same string in Chromium, and `web-videos/<uuid>` appears zero times in any log
sc2_safe_logs.log_level_debug: adds NOTHING on the request path. A boot + login + two reads + a search at LOG_LEVEL=debug produced 20 INFO lines and 0 DEBUG lines; the only DEBUG call sites in the module are in the IPFS mirror (disabled here) and one jobtrace heartbeat-miss line
sc2_safe_logs.recorded_not_fixed: core deliberately logs `object_key` and `storage_key` as structured keys in the media-GC and storage-migration paths, so the platform's posture on a storage key is now inconsistent: jobstatus promises a failure never carries one, and the sweeper logs one on purpose. Worth one ruling, not a unilateral change

sc3_failure_and_metrics.search_table_rows_bug: vidra_search_table_rows reported 0 for ALL FIFTEEN tables while events_inbox held 87 rows, behavior_events 78, query_log 63, query_aggregates 63 and documents 3. Root cause: the source was GREATEST(pg_class.reltuples, 0), and PostgreSQL 14+ writes reltuples = -1 until VACUUM/ANALYZE first touches a relation. last_analyze and last_autoanalyze were null on every one of them. Fixed in search #39

sc4_qoe_source_truth.verdict: PASS, with one privacy question that needs a ruling
sc4_qoe_source_truth.batching: lib/playback-qoe.ts holds an in-memory queue: a full batch of 20 flushes at once, a partial batch waits for a 5s interval tick, and visibilitychange->hidden / pagehide flush with fetch keepalive. A failed POST is DROPPED with no retry. The trap: each flush is an ordinary api.postQoEEvents call, so it mints its own correlation id — a beacon is never correlated with the playback it measured; (video_id, session_id) is the only link
sc4_qoe_source_truth.classification: the client never names a source. It reports source_url (query and fragment stripped client-side — that is where a ?pt= token or a presigned signature lives) and the server classifies the ORIGIN against its own configured bases

measured.case: real HLS playback through this lab's api-proxy delivery
client claims a CDN host with no DELIVERY_CDN_BASE_URL configured
client sends an explicit delivery_source:"cdn" FIELD alongside an api-proxy origin
measured.result: api-proxy — the field is not even read

measured.case: a second api process WITH DELIVERY_CDN_BASE_URL=https://cdn.a35.test, same beacon shape
measured.result: the configured host -> cdn; an unrelated host -> other; https://cdn.a35.test.attacker.example -> OTHER, which is the boundary check a bare HasPrefix would have failed

sc4_qoe_source_truth.cdn_off: the main api, with presign and CDN unconfigured, produced 10 beacons and ZERO cdn rows
sc4_qoe_source_truth.rollup: the hourly worker rolled the walk's hour at 15:05:37 into exactly one row — api-proxy / hls-js / cmaf, event_count 3, start_count 3, verified_count 0, ttff p50 153 / p95 407 / p99 407 ms from a 112-bucket fixed-boundary histogram carrying exactly three marks (the raw TTFFs were 8, 135 and 361 ms)
sc4_qoe_source_truth.admin_surface: GET /admin/qoe/playback-health returns that row in both projections; in Chromium after a hard reload AdminPlaybackHealthView reads `Through the API — Bytes streamed by this server itself`, 3 playbacks, TTFF p50 150 ms p95 410 ms p99 410 ms, Engines: hls.js, Attested 0%, with the sentence explaining that 0% is the expected reading on a public video
sc4_qoe_source_truth.viewer_identity: qoe_events stores viewer_digest — internal/pseudonym's keyed, day-scoped MAC of `u:<account uuid>` when signed in and `ip:<address>` otherwise. The address is never stored. The key derives from JWT_SECRET, so a rotation is also a linkability reset
sc4_qoe_source_truth.optout_finding: the QoE beacon consults NO user preference. a35viewer turned OFF history_enabled, search_history_enabled, personalized_search_enabled and personalized_recommendations_enabled, and their very next playback wrote a qoe_events row carrying the SAME viewer_digest (48e77f473d8f…) as their pre-opt-out rows. Mitigating and worth stating with it: the digest is keyed and day-scoped so it cannot follow a viewer across days or be reversed without the secret, nothing aggregates by viewer, and raw rows live 7 days. It is pseudonymous within-day linkage, not raw attribution — but A13 ruled that an opted-out user must not be attributed in search, and nobody has ruled on whether that reaches playback telemetry

sc5_retention.method: every window is a compile-time constant on an hourly or daily leader-gated tick, so each prune was driven through the SAME exported function the loop calls, against the lab database, by moving the `now` argument the function already takes. No row's timestamp was doctored except where noted

windows.knob: none — deliberate, `an operator-tunable retention is a knob whose wrong setting is discovered months later`
windows.observed: 3 rows survived qoe.Prune at now and at now+6d23h; all 3 deleted at now+7d1h
nothing to delete at now+91d in this window; the batching (10k x 100) and leader gate are unchanged
53 events survived at now; all 53 deleted at now+31d
13 terminal runs survived at now+31d; all 13 deleted at now+91d. Active work is never deleted at any age

windows.window: search_event_retention_days (default 90, validated 1..365), with a 7-day forensic FLOOR for `dead` rows
windows.observed: days=0 is out of range and backstops to 90 (nothing deleted). days=1 at now+2d deleted 8 delivered rows and HELD the dead row. days=1 at now+8d deleted the dead row. `pending` is never pruned at any age

windows.window: 24h ForgetAfter, swept hourly by the heartbeat writer
windows.observed: a planted row for a decommissioned host last seen 25h ago was swept; both live rows kept

PATCH search_event_retention_days=1 in core produced a search.config_updated outbox event, delivered within 8s, and search.service_config carried the new value. The one-shot retention job then deleted exactly the 3 behavior_events past the window and kept the 3 inside it
there is no DELETE against audit_log anywhere in the tree. 34 rows before every prune above, 34 after. This is the finding

sc5_retention.env_shadowing: EVENT_RETENTION_DAYS=1 on the search process changed NOTHING: worker.retention reads the config_updated OVERLAY first and only falls back to the env. The operator path is the instance setting, and the env var is shadowed the moment core has ever pushed a config
sc5_retention.suggestible_reeval: the one-shot refused to run on an emptied ledger with the guard sentence — `suggestible_reeval: skipped — no query_log rows in the retention window; refusing to un-suggest every aggregate on an empty ledger` — which is the A13 behaviour, still holding

The QoE rebuffer, bitrate_switch and error percentiles: a 6-second clip on a loopback origin stalls, switches and fails zero times, so rebuffer_count, bitrate_switch_count and error_count are all 0 and the rebuffer histogram is empty

vidra-search under OpenTelemetry — the service has no OTel to enable

The 30-day job-event and 90-day job-run windows at their real ages — they were exercised by moving the prune's clock argument, not by waiting
findings_not_fixed: search_outbox carries no request/correlation/trace column, so every event that reaches vidra-search asynchronously arrives with a fresh id. Closing it is a migration plus every enqueue path — the same shape A17 ruled on for job_runs — not a surgical change
qoe_events carries no correlation column either; a measurement joins its playback only by (video_id, session_id)
A SUCCESSFUL job writes no correlated worker log line at all. The chain reaches the worker through job_runs/job_events, and through the worker's own log only when something fails
The creator's upload and publish write NO audit_log row, so the audit trail is not on the content-creation path; audit_log.job_id was populated on exactly one row, the admin re-transcode
The worker role builds a metrics registry it can never serve. vidra_search_dead_letters_total is incremented only by the worker-gated drainer
core has no monotonic job-failure counter — only queue-depth and age gauges
audit_log has no retention of any kind
core logs object_key/storage_key as structured keys in the media-GC and storage-migration paths, which is inconsistent with jobstatus's stated invariant now that the failure detail redacts one
vidra-search ships neither logging guard, despite being the service that handles raw query text and despite its logger being a declared TWIN of core's
the QoE beacon ignores the discovery opt-out (see sc4_qoe_source_truth.optout_finding) — a product ruling, not a defect
for_a38: TRANSCODING_MIN_FREE_SCRATCH_MB is the knob that makes a small-disk lab work at all; the shipped floor is 10 GiB and this box had 4.7
`published` is not `playable`: wait on hls_url, not on state
Docker Hub pulls hang here; mirror.gcr.io/<repo> works and can be retagged — that is how the OTel collector ran
zsh's `path` is PATH: a `for path in ...` loop silently destroys the environment mid-script
psql -c with several statements runs them in ONE transaction, so an error in the last one rolls back the first — a doctored timestamp that appears to have been applied may not have been
